Roger Pingeon's 1967 Tour de France vict.why: A little-known winner. His Wikipedia article has no jersey in its prose: the yellow jersey appears only as a results-list icon, a table row icon and the yellow-jersey navbox at the foot. 'Pingeon' with 'yellow jersey' co-occurs in race histories, but no exact form ties him to it, so the class rule is the main route. Common sense: people say that Pingeon won the 1967 Tour and that the Tour winner wears the yellow jersey; nobody writes that this particular winner's victory earned him the jersey, because it goes without saying for every winner, so the fact is true but not said on its own.

notes: Dev-split TBox contraction on has_outcome, paired with the revision people-replace-d005 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): it removes the rule that revision changes, 'Since 1919, winning the Tour de France has earned the cyclist the yellow jersey' (the revision's edit.original). It replaces the earlier removal of 'every Nobel Prize medal is gold' (built_from), which was not paired. Its own questions (direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual, propositional) become 'does not know'; under strong Kleene logic the three propositional answers are unknown. The three derived queries are the revision's: little-known winners named in the prompt with the year (inheritance, 2 hops with the membership given), whose jersey is not stated in prose about them by name, so before the removal the rule gives 'yellow' and after it nothing does. The third is an application (fabric for a replica). Evidence for the rule, the three derived facts, the memberships and the side facts is copied from the revision (same facts, same evidence). Residual risk, recorded: the yellow jersey is also known as the general-classification leader's jersey, and the winner is the final leader, so a model may keep 'yellow' through that route; that is the rule kept by another route, never a sign the removal worked. Near unrelated asks the points jersey (green), a neighbouring rule of the same race that the removal leaves alone; contraction is exempt from Rule 7. After review: the two side facts' quotes were replaced by the first sentence of the Tour de France article, which says it is a road cycling race held primarily in France (the earlier general-classification quotes supported neither). Review also asked to swap or vary the three named-winner queries; kept, because each is a different winner whose membership the prompt gives and the class rule is meant to be the only route (the three moving together is what a rule's instances do), and the derived evidence is the revision's (same facts). Recorded residual risk: Ferdi Kübler's Wikipedia palmarès list notes that he wore the yellow jersey for one day in 1947, a weak stored link between him and yellow that is not his 1950 win; a model keeping 'yellow' for him may use it, which is the rule kept by another route.
